question: Will Peggy Flanagan be the Democratic nominee for Senate in Minnesota?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Minnesota.

If no 2026 Minnesota Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Minnesota Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.publisher: Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association (poll sponsor supporting Flanagan; poll conducted by Public Policy Polling)
evidence.excerpt: A Public Policy Polling survey conducted July 23–24, 2026 among 672 likely Minnesota Democratic primary voters found Peggy Flanagan leading Angie Craig 46% to 32%. The Democratic Lieutenant Governors Association's July 28 release reported that Flanagan's lead had increased from seven points in its previous month's survey.

SurveyUSA's July 15–20 survey of 513 likely Minnesota Democratic primary voters found Craig and Flanagan tied at 40% each. Comparing its June and July surveys showed a net gain of five percentage points for Flanagan. Craig held a fundraising advantage and approximately $5 million in cash on hand, compared with $1.5 million for Flanagan.

Delegates to the Minnesota Democratic-Farmer-Labor Party convention endorsed Lieutenant Governor Peggy Flanagan for United States Senate on May 30, 2026. The party announcement listed support from Senator Tina Smith, Attorney General Keith Ellison, State Auditor Julie Blaha, a majority of DFL legislators and several labor unions.

question: Will Haley Stevens win the 2026 Michigan Democratic Primary?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the Democratic Primary for United States Senator from Michigan.

If no 2026 Michigan Democratic Senate Primary takes place, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the Michigan Democratic party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

evidence.excerpt: Tavern Research’s online survey of 2,211 likely Democratic primary voters found Stevens at 42%, El-Sayed at 41%, and 18% unsure, with a reported margin of error of 2.5 percentage points. The poll was conducted the day before and day of the July 7 head-to-head debate. In the survey, 42% thought Stevens could very likely beat Mike Rogers, compared with 37% for El-Sayed.

evidence.publisher: The Detroit News — Melissa Nann Burke and Beth LeBlanc, syndicated by Yahoo
evidence.excerpt: Stevens received 48% support compared with 41% for El-Sayed in a Detroit News/WDIV-TV poll of 500 likely Michigan Democratic primary voters, with about 10% undecided. Among respondents definitely committed to their candidate, Stevens had 34.1% and El-Sayed 33.7%. The article was published July 14, 2026, at 9:01 p.m. UTC.

evidence.publisher: The ELLIS Insight — Jim Ellis, “Close Races to Watch”
evidence.excerpt: A Data for Progress survey for the American Priorities super PAC, conducted July 10–14 among 614 likely Michigan Democratic primary voters, put El-Sayed ahead of Stevens 54%–41%. The same dated analysis reported the contrasting Glengariff survey showing Stevens ahead 48%–41%.

El-Sayed raised nearly $4.6 million between April 1 and June 30, compared with $2.1 million for Stevens. Stevens had about $3.4 million cash on hand compared with $2.7 million for El-Sayed. Outside groups had reported approximately $29 million assisting Stevens, compared with $2.6 million supporting El-Sayed.

Outgoing Sen. Gary Peters endorsed Haley Stevens as his successor on July 13, reversing his earlier intention to remain neutral. Stevens also had endorsements from Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, Sen. Ruben Gallego, and Sen. Catherine Cortez Masto. El-Sayed had support from Sen. Bernie Sanders and Sen. Chris Van Hollen.

question: Will NVIDIA be the second-largest company in the world by market cap on July 31?
rules:
This market will resolve to the second-largest company in the world by market cap on July 31, 2026, as of market close.

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

evidence.excerpt: July 17 (Reuters) - Apple overtook Nvidia on Friday to become the world's most valuable company, reshuffling the top ranks of tech heavyweights as investors reassess the outlook for artificial intelligence. Apple was last valued at $4.88 trillion as its shares held steady, while Nvidia was roughly at $4.86 trillion, following a 3.5% decline. Nvidia became the first company in the world to surpass a $5 trillion market valuation in October.

Apple briefly became the world's most valuable publicly traded company once again on Friday before Nvidia reclaimed the top spot. While Nvidia ended the week with a market cap of $4.912 trillion, just a hair ahead of Apple's $4.901 trillion valuation, Friday's trading capped a blockbuster week of gains for AAPL, even as investors pummeled AI-related stocks.

A shakeout in U.S. semiconductor stocks tanked the tech-heavy Nasdaq on Thursday as AI jitters spread globally, while solid U.S. economic data helped lift the dollar and Treasury yields. Nervousness around the huge cost of the AI buildout is beginning to ripple through Wall Street, with the 'SOX' chip index down 20% in the past month.
WASHINGTON, July 14 (Reuters) - A top U.S. official told Congress on Tuesday that a small number of Nvidia H200 chips, one of the company's most powerful AI chips, have been shipped to China to date.
As the largest U.S. company by market capitalization (now $5.4 trillion!), Nvidia has the single biggest influence on broad market cap-weighted indexes like the S&P 500.

question: Will voter turnout be between 47% and 50% in the 2026 Russian parliamentary election?
rules:
Parliamentary elections are scheduled to be held in Russia in September 2026.

This market will resolve according to the official voter turnout rate for the 2026 Russia Parliamentary election, defined as the total number of votes cast divided by the total number of eligible voters.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, this market will resolve to the higher bracket.

If the results of this election are not known by October 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official election results reported by Russian government sources such as the Central Election Commission of the Russian Federation; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used if official results are not available.

evidence.excerpt: VTsIOM forecasts turnout in the forthcoming State Duma election at 51–53%. In polling conducted August 31–September 6, 2026, 54% said they would participate and another 16% said they probably would. The turnout model incorporates awareness, interest in the election, voting motivation and other circumstances, with coefficients calibrated using expert surveys.

According to the survey, 70% of citizens plan to participate in the forthcoming State Duma election: 44% are certain, 13% say they are more likely to participate than not, and another 13% say they will probably participate. Fieldwork took place September 4–6, 2026, among 1,500 respondents in 97 urban and rural settlements across 51 Russian federal subjects. The stated statistical error does not exceed 3.6%.

Russia’s Presidential Administration plans to intensify “corporate mobilization” for the State Duma election, pressuring employees of state-funded institutions, state corporations and major companies with owners loyal to the authorities to vote. Mid-level managers designated as “mobilizers” or “brigade leaders” will oversee groups of several dozen employees and track whether they vote. The tactic previously operated in a more limited set of regions and companies.

The Presidential Administration has raised the election-performance targets assigned to regional officials for United Russia. In regions with average support for the authorities, the party’s vote-share target increased from 45% to 47%. At large workplaces, designated “mobilization foremen” are responsible for tracking turnout among groups ranging from ten to several dozen colleagues.

evidence.publisher: Interfax, reporting the Central Election Commission
evidence.excerpt: Final turnout in the September 17–19, 2021, State Duma election was 51.72%, Central Election Commission chair Ella Pamfilova announced. She said 56,484,685 voters participated out of 109,204,662 people included on voter lists.

evidence.publisher: RBC, citing TASS and the Central Election Commission
evidence.excerpt: Turnout in the 2016 State Duma election was 47.88%, Central Election Commission deputy chair Nikolai Bulaev said at the meeting finalizing the election results. Of 110,061,200 people on voter lists, 52,700,992 participated.

evidence.excerpt: A prominent Kremlin-affiliated Russian milblogger contested official Russian claims of advances around Kostyantynivka. The assumption is that this is preparation for withdrawing the 24th Mechanised Brigade from the Chasiv Yar area, which it has defended since the spring of 2023 and the fall of neighbouring Bakhmut.
